items.prompt: What does the Hindi word "नमस्ते" (namaste) mean?

options.label: Hello
Thank you
Excuse me
Please

rubric: नमस्ते is the everyday greeting for hello, and it is also used when parting.
Distractors are other common courtesy words, such as धन्यवाद for thank you.

items.prompt: Which script is Hindi written in?

options.label: Gurmukhi
Bengali
Nastaliq
Devanagari

rubric: Hindi is written in Devanagari.
Gurmukhi (Punjabi), Nastaliq (Urdu) and Bengali are scripts of related languages.

items.prompt: In which direction is Hindi text read?

options.label: Left to right
Top to bottom
Alternating each line
Right to left

rubric: Devanagari runs left to right, with a headline (shirorekha) above the letters.
Right to left is the direction of Urdu, which is a common mix-up.

items.prompt: Which Hindi word means "water"?

options.label: दूध (doodh)
चाय (chai)
पानी (paani)
रोटी (roti)

rubric: पानी is the Hindi word for water.
The other options are milk, tea and bread.

items.prompt: Which Devanagari numeral stands for 5?
rubric: ५ is the Devanagari numeral for 5.
३, ४ and ६ are 3, 4 and 6, and are easy to confuse by shape.

items.prompt: Which of these are vowels (swar) in Devanagari? Select all that apply.

options.label: क
म
इ
अ
उ

rubric: अ, इ and उ are independent vowels.
क and म are consonants (vyanjan).

items.prompt: A new neighbour smiles at you and asks, "आपका नाम क्या है?" You remember this is a standard phrase from your phrasebook. What is the neighbour asking?

options.label: How are you?
What is your name?
Where do you live?
What do you do for work?

rubric: आपका नाम क्या है means What is your name?
Distractors are other get-to-know-you questions that use different phrases.

items.prompt: In the sentence "मैं पढ़ती हूँ" (I read/study), what does the ending "ती" tell you?

options.label: The action happened in the past
The subject is plural
The speaker is female
The sentence is a polite request

rubric: Hindi present-tense verbs agree with the gender of the subject: ता for masculine, ती for feminine.
ती does not mark tense, plurality or politeness.

items.prompt: Which best describes the basic word order of a Hindi sentence?

options.label: Verb–Subject–Object
Subject–Object–Verb
Subject–Verb–Object
Object–Subject–Verb

rubric: Hindi is a subject–object–verb language, as in मैं चाय पीता हूँ.
Subject–verb–object is English word order, which learners often carry over.

items.prompt: You are speaking to your friend's grandmother. Which word for "you" is the appropriate one?

options.label: तू
आप
वह
तुम

rubric: आप is the respectful form for elders and strangers.
तू is very intimate and तुम is informal, so both can sound rude to an elder; वह means he/she.

items.prompt: In "किताब मेज़ पर है", what is the role of the word "पर"?

options.label: It turns the statement into a yes-no question by sitting after the noun
It marks the past tense and comes right before the verb
It makes the noun plural and attaches to the noun
It shows location (on) and follows the noun

rubric: Hindi uses postpositions, which follow the noun; पर means on.
It does not mark tense, number or questions.

items.prompt: What does "मैं कल दिल्ली जाऊँगा" mean?

options.label: I will go to Delhi tomorrow
I used to go to Delhi
I am going to Delhi right now
I went to Delhi yesterday

rubric: कल means both yesterday and tomorrow, so the verb form decides; the future ending ऊँगा gives tomorrow.
Past readings ignore the future ending.

items.prompt: Which sentences have correct verb gender agreement for a female subject? Select all that apply.

options.label: मैं पढ़ती हूँ
वह जाती है
वह जाता है
मैं पढ़ता हूँ

rubric: The ती ending marks a feminine subject.
The ता endings mark masculine subjects.

items.prompt: A learner writes "मैं हूँ भारतीय" to say "I am Indian." Her teacher corrects it to "मैं भारतीय हूँ." Why is the correction needed?

options.label: Hindi puts the verb right after the subject in statements, as English does
Hindi sentences normally end with the verb, even the verb 'to be'
The verb हूँ is only used in questions, never in plain statements
The word भारतीय must always come first in a sentence, before the subject

rubric: Hindi is verb-final, so हूँ goes at the end.
The distractors apply English-style word order or invent rules.

items.prompt: Hindi says 'मेरे पास किताब है' for 'I have a book'. What does this pattern show about how Hindi expresses possession?

options.label: It uses a verb meaning 'to have' that agrees with the speaker
It puts the object before the owner to show emphasis
It adds a special ending to the owner, like 's in English
It uses a place idea: literally 'near me there is a book'

rubric: Hindi usually expresses having with a location phrase such as 'पास' plus 'है'.
Distractors apply English patterns (a 'have' verb, 's ending) to Hindi.

items.prompt: Why does 'अच्छा' change to 'अच्छी' in 'अच्छी लड़की' (good girl)?

options.label: It agrees with the feminine gender of the noun
It shows the noun is plural, as -ई marks many things
It shows extra respect, as -ई is the polite form
It marks the sentence as past tense, as -ई does on verbs

rubric: Adjectives ending in -आ change to -ई with feminine nouns.
Distractors confuse gender agreement with tense, politeness or number.

items.prompt: Which statement best describes the usual word order in 'मैं चाय पीता हूँ' (I drink tea)?

options.label: Verb first, then the subject and the object
Subject–Verb–Object, the same as in English
Object first, then the subject, then the verb
Subject–Object–Verb, with the verb last

rubric: Hindi's default order is Subject–Object–Verb.
Distractors reflect English SVO order or other unusual orders.

items.prompt: What does 'मैं खाना खा रहा हूँ' communicate?

options.label: I am eating food right now
I will eat food later
I ate food earlier today
I eat food every day as a habit

rubric: 'रहा हूँ' marks an action in progress (present continuous).
Distractors mix up habitual, past and future forms.

items.prompt: A learner meets a friend's grandfather for the first time. Which pronoun for 'you' shows the right respect?

options.label: तू
वह
तुम
आप

rubric: 'आप' is the respectful form for elders and strangers.
'तू' is very intimate and 'तुम' is familiar, so both are too casual here.

items.prompt: Hindi uses postpositions, which come after the noun. Which of these words are postpositions? Select all that apply.

options.label: से
क्योंकि
और

rubric: 'में' (in) and 'से' (from/with) follow the noun and link it to the rest of the sentence.
'और' (and) and 'क्योंकि' (because) are conjunctions, not postpositions.

items.prompt: A learner reads 'लड़के स्कूल जाते हैं' and 'लड़कियाँ स्कूल जाती हैं'. Both mean 'go to school' and both are present tense. The learner asks why the verb ending changes from 'जाते' to 'जाती'.

options.label: The ending changes to show the action happened yesterday
The verb agrees with the gender and number of the subject
The ending changes to show the sentence is a question
The ending changes because the school is a different place

rubric: Habitual present verbs agree with the subject's gender and number.
Distractors blame place, mood or tense, which are the same in both sentences.

items.prompt: Choose the correct word to complete: 'वह लड़की बहुत ___ है।' (That girl is very good.)

options.label: अच्छे
अच्छों
अच्छी
अच्छा

rubric: 'लड़की' is feminine singular, so the adjective takes -ई.
'अच्छा' and 'अच्छे' are masculine forms.

items.prompt: A male speaker wants to say 'I am going to the market.' Which sentence is correct?

options.label: मैं बाज़ार जाऊँगी
मैं बाज़ार जा रहा हूँ
मैं बाज़ार जा रहा है
मैं बाज़ार जा रही हूँ

rubric: The masculine speaker needs 'रहा' and the auxiliary 'हूँ' for 'मैं'.
Distractors use the wrong auxiliary, a feminine form or the future tense.

items.prompt: Complete the past-tense sentence: 'कल मैंने रोटी ___।' (Yesterday I ate a roti.)

options.label: खाऊँगी
खाई
खाती हूँ
खाया

rubric: With 'ने' the verb agrees with the object, and 'रोटी' is feminine, so 'खाई'.
'खाया' agrees with the speaker or a masculine object instead.

items.prompt: Which Hindi number word means 47?

options.label: सत्तावन
सत्तासी
सैंतालीस
सैंतीस

rubric: सैंतालीस is 47.
The others are 37, 57 and 87, which sound similar.

items.prompt: Which Devanagari spelling is read 'doodh' (milk), with a long 'oo' vowel?

options.label: दूद
धूद
दूध
दुध

rubric: दूध has the long ू matra and the letters द and ध in order.
'दुध' has a short vowel; 'दूद' and 'धूद' swap or change consonants.

items.prompt: Which sentences correctly complete 'मेरे पास ___ हैं।' with a plural verb and matching noun? Select all that apply.

options.label: दो किताबें
एक कुर्सी
एक घड़ी
तीन पेन

rubric: Plural objects ('दो किताबें', 'तीन पेन') agree with 'हैं'.
'एक घड़ी' and 'एक कुर्सी' are singular and would need 'है'.

items.prompt: You are at a railway platform and want to ask an older stranger where the station exit is. You want to be polite and speak as a man.

options.label: क्या आप बता सकते हैं, निकास कहाँ है?
तुम बताओ, निकास कहाँ है?
तू बता, निकास कहाँ है?
क्या आप बता सकता है, निकास कहाँ है?

rubric: 'आप' takes the plural verb forms 'सकते हैं', which is the polite pattern.
Distractors use 'तू' or 'तुम', or pair 'आप' with a singular verb.

items.prompt: Choose the correct Hindi for 'Ram ate the bread' (simple past, roti is feminine).

options.label: राम ने रोटी खाई
राम ने रोटी खाया
राम को रोटी खाई
राम रोटी खाई

rubric: In the past tense of a transitive verb the subject takes ने and the verb agrees with the object रोटी (feminine), giving खाई.
खाया ignores object agreement; dropping ने or using को breaks the construction.

items.prompt: How do you say 'to the boys' in Hindi?

options.label: लड़का को
लड़के को
लड़कें को
लड़कों को

rubric: A plural noun before a postposition takes the oblique plural ending -ों: लड़कों को.
लड़के को is the oblique singular; लड़का को leaves the noun in the direct form.

items.prompt: Choose the correct Hindi for 'She will go tomorrow.'

options.label: वह कल जाती है
वह कल गई होगी
वह कल जाएगी
वह कल जाएगा

rubric: The future uses the -ए/-एगी endings and agrees with a feminine subject: जाएगी.
जाएगा is masculine; the other options are habitual present or a past supposition.

items.prompt: Choose the correct Hindi for 'I have a sister.'

options.label: मैं एक बहन है
मुझे एक बहन है
मेरी एक बहन है
मेरा एक बहन है

rubric: Possession of a relative uses the possessive pronoun agreeing with the possessed noun: मेरी बहन (feminine).
मेरा mismatches gender; मैं and मुझे do not form the possessive pattern.

items.prompt: Choose the correct Hindi for 'Rohan does not eat meat' (habit, as a general fact).

options.label: रोहन मांस नहीं खाता
रोहन मांस मत खाता
रोहन मांस नहीं खाया
रोहन मांस नहीं खाती

rubric: The habitual form with a masculine subject is खाता, negated with नहीं.
खाती is feminine, खाया is past, and मत is used only for prohibitions.

items.prompt: Which sentences are grammatically correct in the simple past? Select all that apply.

options.label: मैंने किताब पढ़ा
उसने खाना खाई
लड़कियाँ स्कूल गईं
मैंने किताब पढ़ी

rubric: With ने the verb agrees with the unmarked object (किताब is feminine, so पढ़ी); intransitive गईं agrees with the plural feminine subject.
खाना is masculine so खाई is wrong, and पढ़ा mismatches किताब.

items.prompt: You are visiting your friend's grandmother for the first time. She has just welcomed you into the living room and you want to politely invite her to sit down with you. Which sentence is most appropriate?

options.label: आप बैठो, दादी जी।
तू बैठ, दादी जी।
आप बैठिए, दादी जी।
तुम बैठो, दादी जी।

rubric: An elder calls for the respectful आप with the honorific imperative बैठिए.
तू and तुम are too familiar, and आप with बैठो mixes registers.

items.prompt: A learner writes 'मैंने रोटी खाया'. What is the underlying error?

options.label: खाया should become खाता, because a past action with ने needs the habitual form of the verb
The verb should agree with the object रोटी, so it must be खाई
The verb should agree with the subject मैं, so खाया is right but रोटी should be treated as a masculine noun here
ने should be dropped, because the first person subject मैं does not take ने in the simple past tense

rubric: In ने-constructions the verb agrees with the unmarked object, here the feminine रोटी.
Distractors assume agreement with the subject or that ने is optional.

items.prompt: Compare 'वह रोज़ चाय पीता है' and 'वह चाय पी रहा है'. What is the key difference?

options.label: The first has a plural subject, since पीता ends in the vowel -ा and signals many drinkers
The first is formal and the second casual, because रहा marks respect toward the listener
The first states a routine, while the second describes an action happening now
The first is past and the second present, since पीता is a past form of the verb and रहा is not

rubric: The habitual present expresses routine; the -रहा है construction expresses an ongoing action.
Distractors confuse aspect with tense, register or number.

items.prompt: A learner reads 'स्कूल' aloud as 'sakool', inserting an extra vowel. What is the cause?

options.label: The learner read the conjunct स्क with an inherent 'a' after स instead of joined sounds
The learner took the first letter as a vowel sign because it sits above the line
The learner confused ल with a retroflex consonant and added a vowel before it
The learner treated the vowel ू as a short vowel and changed the second syllable

rubric: In a conjunct the first consonant has no inherent vowel, so स्क is read 'sk'.
The other options blame vowel length or letter shape, which do not produce the extra syllable.

items.prompt: A learner writes 'मेरा भाई की गाड़ी' for 'my brother's car'. Which correction and reason are right?

options.label: मेरी भाई की गाड़ी, because मेरा must agree with the feminine गाड़ी that is possessed, not with भाई
मेरे भाई की गाड़ी, because भाई is oblique before की so मेरा becomes मेरे, and की agrees with गाड़ी
मेरा भाई का गाड़ी, because का is the default possessive and stays the same for every possessed noun
मेरे भाई का गाड़ी, because भाई is plural here, so मेरे is needed and का follows the speaker

rubric: The noun before a postposition is oblique, so its modifier takes -े, while की agrees with the possessed noun गाड़ी.
Distractors apply agreement with the wrong noun or treat का as invariable.

items.prompt: A learner writes 'मैंने घर गया' for 'I went home'. Why is it wrong?

options.label: जाना is intransitive, so the subject takes no ने: मैं घर गया
घर is a destination, so it needs the postposition को: मैंने घर को गया
गया should become गई, because the perfective verb agrees with the noun घर
ने is correct here, but the verb must change to the present form: मैंने घर जाता हूँ

rubric: ने appears with transitive verbs in the perfective; जाना is intransitive, so the subject is unmarked.
Distractors invent object marking or misapply agreement.

items.prompt: Which statements correctly analyse the difference between 'तू जा', 'तुम जाओ' and 'आप जाइए'? Select all that apply.

options.label: आप जाइए is the respectful form suited to elders or strangers
The three differ only in spelling, not in politeness
तुम जाओ is the right choice for addressing a respected elder
तू is very intimate and can sound rude with strangers

rubric: Hindi marks politeness through pronoun and verb ending: तू intimate, तुम familiar, आप respectful.
तुम is not respectful enough for elders, and the forms differ in register, not spelling.

items.prompt: A learner translates 'I was reading a book when he came' as 'मैं किताब पढ़ता है जब वह आया'. Their teacher wants to find the main error in the first clause.

options.label: It needs the past progressive पढ़ रहा था, not a habitual present
किताब is the object, so the verb needs ने and the clause should begin with मैंने
जब should be कब, since the clause says when the reading happened
आया should be future, because the reading was still going on then

rubric: An action in progress in the past needs पढ़ रहा था; पढ़ता है is habitual present and also mismatches मैं.
ने does not appear with progressive forms, and जब correctly means 'when' here.

items.prompt: In the sentence `मुझे हिन्दी आती है।`, the verb ends in the feminine `-ती` even when the speaker is a man. Which analysis explains this?

options.label: आना agrees with the speaker, and मुझे is a feminine pronoun that forces feminine endings
आना agrees with हिन्दी, the real grammatical subject, and not with the person marked by मुझे
आना agrees with मुझे, and the verb takes its feminine default form after any dative pronoun
आती is feminine because the names of languages always force feminine verb endings in Hindi

rubric: In the dative-subject construction the verb agrees with the unmarked noun हिन्दी, not the experiencer.
The distractors treat agreement as driven by the speaker or by a blanket rule about languages.

items.prompt: A learner writes `सीता ने खाना बनाई।` and a teacher marks the verb as wrong. What is the fault and its cause?

options.label: ने should be dropped, because बनाना is intransitive and so the verb agrees with the subject सीता
बनाई should be बनाए, because खाना is treated as plural and so the verb must take the plural ending
बनाई is correct, because the verb always agrees with the feminine subject सीता even after ने
बनाई should be बनाया, because खाना is masculine and the verb agrees with the unmarked object

rubric: With ने in the perfective, the verb agrees with the unmarked object, and खाना is masculine singular.
The strongest distractor keeps agreement with the subject, which is the pattern ने blocks.

items.prompt: In `मैं बड़े शहर में रहता हूँ।`, the adjective is `बड़े` and not `बड़ा`, though only one city is meant. Which analysis is correct?

options.label: बड़े shows plural, because a big city implies many people living in it
बड़े is used because the postposition में always requires a plural form of any adjective before it
बड़े is a polite form that is used for places, and the plain form बड़ा is reserved for people
बड़े appears because शहर is in the oblique before में, so the masculine adjective changes its ending

rubric: A masculine -आ adjective takes -ए when its noun is oblique before a postposition.
Distractors confuse the oblique change with plurality or politeness.

items.prompt: In `धर्म`, the sound र comes before म, yet it is written as a small hook above म. Which analysis explains this?

options.label: The hook is a halant that has been moved onto म so that ध can keep its inherent vowel sound
A vowelless र before another consonant is written as a hook on the next letter
The hook is a vowel sign showing that म is followed by a short vowel sound in speech
The hook is a nasalisation mark like a chandrabindu and it changes how म is pronounced

rubric: A vowelless र before a consonant is written as the repha above the next letter.
Distractors mistake it for a vowel sign, a nasal mark or a displaced halant.

items.prompt: Compare `उसने खाना खाया।` with `उसने खाना खा लिया।` What does the added `लिया` contribute?

options.label: It shows that someone else received the food, so it marks a beneficiary
It adds a sense of completion, and the action is seen as done through to the end
It makes the request more polite, because लेना is the honorific form of खाना
It turns the sentence into the past perfect, so it means 'he had eaten'

rubric: A compound verb with लेना adds completion and often self-benefit.
Distractors mistake it for tense, a beneficiary or honorific marking.

items.prompt: Which of these sentences are grammatically correct in standard Hindi? Select all that apply.

options.label: उसने चिट्ठी लिखी।
राम ने कहानी सुनाया।
औरतें पानी पीती है।
लड़कियाँ बाज़ार गईं।

rubric: चिट्ठी is feminine, so लिखी is right after ने, and गईं agrees with the feminine plural subject.
In the wrong options, सुनाया ignores the feminine कहानी and है ignores the plural subject.

items.prompt: A learner who has been in Mumbai for a week says to the elderly owner of his guesthouse: `तुम मुझे चाबी दो।` His grammar is correct, yet the owner stiffens and answers curtly. Which analysis best explains the reaction?

options.label: चाबी is feminine, so दो should be दी, and the owner is reacting to the agreement error
The verb should come before the object in a request, and the odd word order sounded rude
तुम with a bare imperative is a familiar register, which is too casual for an older stranger
मुझे is the wrong form in a request, and मैं should have been used with the imperative

rubric: The pronoun तुम and the plain imperative दो are too familiar for an elderly stranger; आप with दीजिए fits.
The distractors invent agreement or word-order faults in a correct sentence.

items.prompt: You want to say 'I have been living in Delhi for five years', and it is still true now. Judged against that criterion, which sentence is best?

options.label: मैं पाँच साल पहले दिल्ली में रहा था।
मैं पाँच साल से दिल्ली में रह रहा हूँ।
मैं पाँच साल तक दिल्ली में रहूँगा।
मैं पाँच साल दिल्ली में रह चुका था।

rubric: से with the present continuous marks an action that began in the past and continues now.
The others describe a finished past, a future, or a completed past state.

items.prompt: A learner has three months to read bus boards and menus in Delhi and wants to avoid fossilised pronunciation errors. Judged by these criteria, which plan is best?

options.label: Start with romanisation for six months, since the script slows speaking and can be added at the end
Learn Devanagari first, since its letter-sound mapping is regular and signs cannot be read in romanisation
Use romanisation alone, because its spelling maps one-to-one onto Hindi sounds and signs can be guessed
Learn the twenty commonest letters only, because context lets you guess the rest and skip vowel signs

rubric: Reading real signs needs the script, and Devanagari's regular mapping also trains accurate pronunciation.
Romanisation is inconsistent, and partial script knowledge fails on unfamiliar words.

items.prompt: Two learners explain the choice among का/की/के in `लड़की का भाई` and `मेरी माँ का घर`. A says it agrees with the possessor. B says it agrees with the thing possessed. Which explanation is better supported by both examples?

options.label: A, because the possessor's gender decides it, and the feminine owners here are the cause of the choice
A, because का follows लड़की and माँ, which are the owners and decide the form
Neither, because का is a fixed form and the variation is only a spelling convention
B, because का follows भाई and घर, which are masculine, though both possessors are feminine

rubric: In both examples the possessors are feminine yet का appears, so it must agree with the masculine possessed noun.
A fails on the data, and the claim that का is fixed ignores की and के.

items.prompt: A learner says: 'Devanagari is perfectly phonetic, so I pronounce every letter, including the inherent a, in each word.' Which critique is most accurate?

options.label: The claim is false, because each letter takes several sounds depending on its position in the word
The claim is false, because the script writes only consonants and the reader must supply the vowels
The script is largely regular, but the inherent a is often dropped, as in कमल read 'kamal'
The claim holds, and कमल is correctly read 'kamala' with the final a pronounced

rubric: Devanagari is regular, but schwa deletion means the inherent a is not always pronounced, especially word-finally.
The distractors overstate or invert the irregularity.

items.prompt: A learner plans to master `ने` by memorising a list of verbs that take it. Judged by the criteria of working on new verbs and low long-term effort, which advice is best?

options.label: Keep the list, since ने is assigned verb by verb and there is no pattern that would carry over to verbs not yet met
Use ने whenever the subject is third person, since it marks person rather than tense or transitivity of the verb
Use ने in every past-tense sentence, treating intransitive and transitive verbs alike, since it simply marks past tense
Learn that ने marks the subject of transitive verbs in perfective tenses, and note exceptions as they appear

rubric: A rule tied to transitivity and the perfective generalises to new verbs, with a few exceptions to note.
Distractors say there is no pattern or apply the wrong trigger.

items.prompt: A teacher has limited time and wants to drill only slips that turn one everyday word into a different word. Which pairs justify priority drilling? Select all that apply.

options.label: क़ीमत pronounced as कीमत
दाल (lentils) pronounced as डाल (branch)
पल (moment) pronounced as फल (fruit)
ज़रा pronounced as जरा

rubric: Aspiration and dental versus retroflex contrasts separate different words.
The ज़/ज and क़/क slips are common but rarely change which word is understood.

items.prompt: Your landlord, an older man you have met twice, has not fixed a leaking tap. You will text him in Devanagari. The message must be respectful, make a clear request and sound natural, not stiff. Which message best meets all three?

options.label: आपका नल टपक रहा है, इसे ठीक करवाना आपकी ज़िम्मेदारी है।
नमस्ते जी, कृपया नल ठीक करवा दीजिए, वह टपक रहा है।
नल टपक रहा है, तू जल्दी से ठीक करवा दे।
तुम नल ठीक करवा दो, वह बहुत टपक रहा है।

rubric: कृपया with दीजिए is respectful and a clear request, and the greeting keeps it natural.
तू and तुम are too familiar, and the last option is accusatory rather than a polite request.

items.prompt: A teacher explains the sentence 'मुझे हिंदी आती है' (I know Hindi). Which analysis best accounts for the verb form आती?

options.label: आती agrees with हिंदी, the nominative argument; मुझे only marks the experiencer and never controls agreement.
आती agrees with मुझे, which acts as the subject here, so the form shows that the speaker is a woman.
आती is feminine because आना takes feminine endings whenever it expresses knowing a skill or language.
आती agrees with whichever noun stands closest to the verb, regardless of that noun's grammatical role.

rubric: In dative-subject constructions the verb agrees with the nominative thing known, here हिंदी, which is feminine.
Distractors treat मुझे as the agreement controller or invent verb-specific or proximity rules.

items.prompt: A railway station wants a printed Hindi notice asking all passengers, strangers of any age, to wait in the queue. Criteria: formal, polite, and consistent in address form. Which wording is best?

options.label: तू पंक्ति में प्रतीक्षा कर।
आप पंक्ति में प्रतीक्षा करो।
कृपया पंक्ति में प्रतीक्षा करो।
कृपया पंक्ति में प्रतीक्षा करें।

rubric: The आप-level imperative in -एँ with कृपया is the standard formal public register.
Distractors mix आप with तुम forms, use तुम with strangers, or use the intimate तू form.

items.prompt: Judged by how native speakers normally express kinship, which Hindi sentence is the most idiomatic way to say 'I have an older brother'?

options.label: मेरे पास एक बड़ा भाई है।
मेरा एक बड़ा भाई है।
मैं एक बड़ा भाई रखता हूँ।
मुझे एक बड़ा भाई है।

rubric: Kin and relationships take the possessive का construction, not पास, which suggests physical or material possession.
Distractors transfer English 'have' through पास, a wrongly used dative, or a literal verb.

items.prompt: Someone moved to Delhi three years ago and still lives there. Judging by tense and aspect, which sentence best says 'I have been living in Delhi for three years'?

options.label: मैं तीन साल दिल्ली में रहा।
मैं तीन साल से दिल्ली में रह रहा हूँ।
मैं तीन साल के लिए दिल्ली में रहूँगा।
मैं तीन साल से दिल्ली में रहा था।

rubric: Present continuous with से expresses an action that began in the past and continues now.
Distractors give a finished past, a future plan, or a pluperfect that implies the stay is over.

items.prompt: A student insists that every Hindi adjective must change with the noun's gender and 'corrects' सुंदर लड़की to सुंदरी लड़की. Which critique is most accurate?

options.label: Adjectives agree only in number and never in gender, so अच्छी लड़की is wrong and सुंदर लड़की is right.
Only -ā adjectives like अच्छा inflect; consonant-final ones like सुंदर stay unchanged, so the original was right.
Consonant-final adjectives inflect only for plural, so सुंदर लड़की is wrong but सुंदर लड़कियाँ would be correct.
The student is right, since a feminine noun always needs an adjective ending in -ī before it.

rubric: Only adjectives ending in -ā inflect for gender, number and case; consonant-final adjectives are invariable.
Distractors overgeneralise the -ī pattern or invent number-only agreement.

items.prompt: Judging oblique-case agreement before postpositions, which phrases are correctly formed? Select all that apply.

options.label: छोटा कमरे में
उस लड़कों को
छोटे कमरे में
उन लड़कों के साथ

rubric: Demonstrative, adjective and noun all take oblique forms before a postposition, and they must agree in number.
Distractors leave the adjective in the direct case or mix singular उस with a plural noun.

items.prompt: Meera wants to tell a friend she will go to Delhi tomorrow if it does not rain, which is a real possibility. Her draft reads 'अगर कल बारिश नहीं होती तो मैं जाऊँगी।' A tutor says the condition clause has the wrong form for a real possibility. Which revision is best?

options.label: अगर कल बारिश नहीं हुई तो मैं जाऊँगी।
अगर कल बारिश नहीं हुई थी तो मैं जाऊँगी।
अगर कल बारिश नहीं होती तो मैं जाती।
अगर कल बारिश नहीं हो रही तो मैं जाऊँगी।

rubric: A real future possibility uses the simple perfective in the अगर clause with a future main clause.
The -ती...-ती pattern marks a contrary-to-fact condition, and the other options mismatch aspect with the future.

items.prompt: You must assemble one sentence asking a staff member to politely tell a respected visiting professor (third person) to come tomorrow. Which sentence meets every constraint?

options.label: कृपया उनसे कल आने के लिए कहता।
कृपया उनसे कल आने के लिए कहिए।
कृपया उनसे कल आने के लिए कहो।
कृपया उससे कल आने के लिए कहिए।

rubric: उनसे gives honorific reference to the professor and कहिए gives the polite imperative to the staff member.
Distractors use the non-honorific उससे, the familiar कहो, or an incomplete verb form.

items.prompt: You are designing a listening drill where each word pair differs only in consonant aspiration. Which set of pairs meets that constraint?

options.label: कल–कर, पल–पर, गम–गल
दाल–डाल, तार–टार, दम–डम
पल–फल, बाल–भाल, गाना–घाना
पल–पाल, बल–बाल, कम–काम

rubric: Each pair contrasts an unaspirated stop with its aspirated counterpart and nothing else.
Distractors contrast vowel length, dental versus retroflex place, or entirely different consonants.

items.prompt: You need a natural Hindi sentence for a tired speaker who means 'I can't walk any more' using the idiom of incapacity (not a simple ability statement). Which sentence meets that requirement?

options.label: मुझसे अब चला नहीं जाता।
मैं अब चलता नहीं सकता।
मुझे अब चलना नहीं जाता।
मुझसे अब चलना नहीं सकता।

rubric: The idiom pairs instrumental-subject मुझसे with the perfective participle plus जाना, here चला नहीं जाता.
Distractors scramble सकना, which follows the verb root, or apply the knowing construction to walking.

items.prompt: A learner drafts the rule 'The Hindi verb always agrees with the subject in gender and number.' Which addition best repairs the rule so it covers the perfective tenses?

options.label: In the perfective, the verb agrees with the indirect object marked by को, since that is the receiver of the action.
In the perfective, the verb takes the masculine singular form with every subject, since the tense has lost its agreement.
In the perfective, the verb agrees with the subject only if it is feminine or plural, otherwise it stays neutral.
In the perfective of transitive verbs, a ने-marked subject is skipped and the verb agrees with the unmarked object.

rubric: Ergative alignment makes the verb agree with the unmarked object, and default masculine singular when none is available.
Distractors invent agreement with feminine or plural subjects, a blanket masculine default, or an indirect object.

items.prompt: You are assembling a sentence meaning 'The book that you gave me is very good', with a relative-correlative structure and correct agreement. Which sentence meets all the constraints?

options.label: जो किताब आपने मुझे दी, वह बहुत अच्छा है।
जो किताब आपने मुझे दी, वह बहुत अच्छी है।
जो किताब आपने मुझे दिया, वह बहुत अच्छी है।
जो किताब आपको मुझे दी, वह बहुत अच्छी है।

rubric: दी agrees with the feminine object किताब, since the ने subject is skipped, and अच्छी agrees with वह किताब.
Distractors break verb agreement, adjective agreement, or the ergative marking of the giver.

items.prompt: You want a sentence meaning 'He has finished reading the book' (completed action, male subject) using completive forms. Which sentences meet this requirement? Select all that apply.

options.label: वह किताब पढ़ चुकी है।
उसने किताब पढ़ ली।
उसने किताब पढ़ दी।
वह किताब पढ़ चुका है।

rubric: पढ़ लेना with ने and पढ़ चुकना both mark completion, and चुका agrees with a male subject.
पढ़ देना means reading for someone else, and चुकी requires a female subject.

items.prompt: A Hindi app must confirm 'You have been registered' to users whose gender it does not know. Constraints: polite आप address, and no verb or participle form that reveals the user's gender. Which template satisfies both?

options.label: आप पंजीकृत हो गई हैं।
आप पंजीकृत हो गए हैं।
आप पंजीकृत हो चुके हैं।
आपका पंजीकरण हो गया है।

rubric: Making पंजीकरण the grammatical subject means the verb agrees with a neutral noun, not the user.
The other options use हो चुके, हो गई or हो गए, which mark the user as masculine or feminine.
